title: Nearby ozone sites had 25-75% positive agreement on three-day episodes above 70 ppb before selected US bird surveys in 2005-2019
abstract: We tested whether two nearby ozone sites gave the same three-day episode status in the month before a bird survey. We used 1,599 selected windows in California, Oregon, New York, and Pennsylvania in 2005-2019. Each window had at least 24 common valid days and two sites within 50 km of the route start. Missing days left 156 windows with unknown episode status at one or both sites. Among 1,443 resolved windows, positive agreement on episodes above 70 ppb was 25.0-75.4% across two regions and two periods. Overall disagreement was 1.1-10.9%. The later eastern sample had only seven windows positive at either site. Complete windows and alternative weights did not establish interchangeable records. These are finite-sample exposure measures. Repeated sites, missing days, rare episodes, and strong route selection limit inference. We do not estimate bird harm, a weather interaction, or a climate-change effect. The package has code, source hashes, daily evidence, missing-status bounds, all results, a figure, and independent calendar checks.

display.caption: Positive agreement and resolved-status coverage for episodes of one, two, three, or five consecutive days above 70 ppb. Missing days do not join separate runs. Lines describe selected finite samples and have no population confidence intervals.

citations.reason: Verified source of the route windows, paired daily site data, raw retrieval code, and source provenance. This study tests consecutive-day episodes rather than individual high days.
